_about: The bell tower: Orin's echo and the final choice.
tower_bell: The great bell hangs above you, cracked from shoulder to lip. Blue light pulses deep inside it, slow as breathing.
Around its waist, thirteen marks. Twelve are dull bronze. The last one glows faintly blue.
tower_desk: Orin's desk. Candle stubs, ink, and a stack of notes in his cramped, careful hand.

tower_desk.text: He taught me the song. At the well, when I was small. That's why I knew how it ended.
He taught me a song once? I don't remember it. Somebody in Dawnmere must.

tower_chair: Orin's chair. The cushion still holds his shape, as if he only stood up a moment ago.
tower_window: Far below, Dawnmere's lanterns burn in a small, brave ring. Beyond them, the mist is a grey tide, rising.
tower_memories_echo: The bell's light spills out, and you see them: memories, crowded inside the bronze like moths in a jar.
A girl laughing loud enough to fill the tower. A woman singing over a cradle. Two young people carving names into a well. A monk tearing pages from a book. A boy in borrowed armour, guarding a road.

tower_memories_echo.text: Tobin and Elsie. She's in there, and her lamp is still lit down in the square.

tower_memories_echo: Everything Dawnmere gave away. It's all still in there.
tower_mechanism: The bell's mechanism: a great iron wheel, cracked and jammed on its own broken teeth. In the hub, an empty slot.
The pin slides home. Iron grinds against iron, and the whole tower shudders awake.
orin: I suppose there are advantages to being a memory.
I tried to stop the bell.
Because I finally remembered what it had already taken.
My daughter had a laugh that could fill this whole tower.
But I cannot remember the sound.
Because every night I was given a choice.
Let the mist find the village...
...or let the bell take something small enough that we could pretend nothing had changed.

choice.text: Whose voice did the bell borrow?
There was a watchman at the crossing.

orin: It's in here. With all the others. It went the night her boy had the fever. I let the bell take it, because I thought she'd rather have him well than have the song.
I was right. And I was wrong. Both at once. That is the bell's whole trick.
...The Sentinel told you to ask that. He always was the cleverest of us.

orin.text: But you already know. The village's own. Thirteen notes, sung together at dusk.
The village's. Before the bell, everyone gathered at dusk and sang. Thirteen notes. The mist can't take hold of a village that's holding on to itself.

orin: Singing every night, in the cold, all of us... it was hard. So we cast a bell to sing for us. And a bell has no memories of its own to spend.
Because you were away. The bell couldn't reach you. You're the only one in Dawnmere who still has all of yourself.

orin.text: I taught you the old song once. At the well. You were seven, and you sang it flat.
You've read my notes, so you know about the song. You were seven. You sang it flat.
I remember. Pip hummed it, and I knew how it ended.
No. Perhaps someone else in Dawnmere still does.

orin: Edrin. He kept that crossing longer than I've kept this tower.
One night he asked me who he was waiting for. I didn't know. I'm not sure anyone did, by then.
Then the bell didn't take everything. It never quite does.
orin_after: The bell is still listening, Rowan. So am I.
orin_decide: The old mechanism can be repaired.
One more toll will turn the mist away.
And whose memory will it take?

orin_decide.text: There's another way. Thirteen marks. Thirteen notes. The pin can tune it.
...You remember the song. Then the last mark isn't a toll at all. It's the end of the tune. The note that gives back.

choice.text: Ring the bell. Pay the price.
Break the bell. End the bargain.
Retune the bell. Sing the thirteenth note.

orin_decide: Then let it be the last thing you ever give it. And Rowan... thank you for coming home.
They'll be frightened. They'll be cold. But they'll be themselves.
Give them a reason to remember why. And Rowan... thank you for coming home.
Thirteen notes. Sing it flat, like you used to. The bell won't mind.
Take your time. The bell has waited this long. It can wait for you.
